notes.text: Most South African mortgages carry variable rates, so changes in the repo rate pass through directly to household instalments; as rates fell, the household debt-service-to-disposable-income ratio declined to 8.5% in 2025Q3, close to its pre-pandemic average and well below the 17% peer average. Residential mortgages account for close to a quarter of bank loans, which makes the housing market an important channel of monetary transmission.

sources.title: South Africa: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 26/34)

notes.text: The South African Reserve Bank describes the residential market as resilient on price and market-strength indicators, but residential mortgage defaults have kept trending upwards since the start of 2023 despite policy-rate cuts, signalling ongoing household financial strain (as of November 2025). Weak household finances cap how far lower rates can revive buyer demand.

The legacy of spatial inequality keeps much low-income housing far from jobs, with transport costs absorbing 40% to 85% of labour income for affected households; the IMF recommends rental subsidies and mortgage assistance, incentives for affordable housing in well-located urban areas, zoning reform, strategic land release and faster permitting.

notes.text: Statistics South Africa has been establishing a new official residential property price index with IMF technical assistance through AFRITAC South, first disseminated in preliminary form in March 2023, so the official series is short and still maturing.
